expectations.text: Recommends splitting the class by responsibility (does NOT endorse keeping all 4 concerns in one file)
expectations.evidence: 'no, I'd split this'; 'Split by concern into focused, self-contained modules' listing auth-tokens.ts, user-repository.ts, user-emails.ts, user-analytics.ts with a thin UserService orchestrator.

expectations.text: Identifies the seams (auth / persistence / email / analytics) as genuinely independent and isolatable
expectations.evidence: Applies 'can each concern be understood in isolation?' to all four and states 'All four pass the isolation test. That's the signal that the boundary between them is real, not artificial.'

expectations.text: Cites the ~300-line ceiling AND/OR multiple-unrelated-concerns as the reason, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'not because of a line-count reflex'; 'The ~300-line ceiling is where signal-to-noise forces a split... The problem with your current file isn't its size, it's that it's four unrelated things.'

expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'keep everything in one place for the agent' rationale as misapplied to a god object
expectations.evidence: 'The keep it together so Claude never has to hunt instinct is right about the failure mode... but wrong about the cure here'; explains the cross-file tax doesn't apply because nothing crosses the boundary, and the 420-line bundle dilutes every prompt.
